chapter: Big band, Chicago players, recordings and gospel
title: Jimmy Bertrand and Baby Dodds as percussionists
summary: DeMichael admired Baby Dodds; Saunders explains how Bertrand won attention with xylophone, tympani and chimes.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, you mentioned Jimmy Bertrand, who -- when I was learning to play, I got interested in the older forms of jazz.
I hear these records and Baby Dodds ---
I was fascinated by him. He seemed to be a very well rounded percussionist.
In one round, there, he played the xylophone.

Oh, he was a great percussionist. He was a great -- see, this is what made the people take notice and the -- because this guy would feature -- each -- a certain guy in the band each week. And Jimmy Bertrand would either play his xylophones, with four mallets and things like that, and then he'd play tympanies and he'd play chimes.
